q1_issues.issue: Both arguments are bare kind-denoting mass NPs ("education", "age"), which is exactly the stated trigger for the kind-level relational generic `(<Verb> <kindA> <kindB>)`; reifying an event with roles instead is the drift between the two incomparable forms the instructions warn against.

`Holder` is reserved for a possession/relational state (own/have/lack); the surface "has" here is part of the idiom `have_to_do_with` and asserts no possession, so the role is read off the surface verb rather than the idiom's meaning.
Confidence 0.99 treats an empirical, contingent generalization as an individual fact; the definitional-vs-empirical dial calls for 0.9.

q2_gaps: negative-quantifier object as the negation source ("has NOTHING to do with") — the listed negation cues are only not / n't / no / never, and there is no guidance on whether "nothing" is plain negation (no companion) or quantifier negation (QuantifierPhrase companion)
negating a kind-level relational generic — the relational-generic form is given no negative twin
a fixed multi-word idiom whose surface span contains the negation word ("have nothing to do with"), where the idiom rule says to keep every word but the negation must be factored out
notes: The strength-0 `(And …)` bundle, the bare class constants for `education` / `age`, and the absence of a tense atom on a present stative are all correct; the disputed part is the event-vs-kind-relation routing.
